note: Why does my useEffect run twice in development? StrictMode intentionally double-invokes effects to surface missing cleanup. It only happens in dev builds.
Promise.all rejects on the first failure -- use Promise.allSettled when you need every result regardless of individual errors.
Center a div: set the parent to display:flex with justify-content:center and align-items:center. Works every time.
@State vs @Binding: @State owns the value; @Binding is a two-way reference passed to a child so it can mutate the parent's state.
Keys should be stable IDs, not array indexes; index keys cause the wrong item to be reused when a list reorders.
Why is `this` undefined in a method passed as a callback? Bind it or use an arrow-function field; a standalone method reference loses its receiver.
Grid vs flexbox: flexbox is one-dimensional (a row or a column); grid is two-dimensional (rows and columns at once).
Pushing a new screen: use NavigationStack + NavigationLink. NavigationView is deprecated as of iOS 16.
z-index not working? It only applies to positioned elements, and it is scoped by its stacking context.
Component re-renders too often -- wrap expensive children in React.memo and memoize callbacks with useCallback so their props stay referentially stable.
Debounce vs throttle: debounce fires after activity stops (a search box); throttle fires at most once per interval (scroll handlers).
List not updating? The model needs to be a class conforming to ObservableObject with @Published properties.
Use gap instead of margins to space flex and grid children -- no more last-child margin hacks.
Optional chaining a?.b?.c short-circuits to undefined instead of throwing when something is null or undefined.
Lifting state up vs context: reach for context only for truly global values like theme or auth; overusing it re-renders everything below.
Animate a change by wrapping the mutation in withAnimation { } or attaching .animation(_:value:) to the view.
Avoid stale state in a setInterval callback by using the functional updater setCount(c => c + 1) or a ref instead of the captured value.
Sticky header: use position: sticky with top: 0, and make sure no ancestor has overflow hidden or it silently stops working.
Keep the SwiftUI body cheap -- it recomputes often; move heavy work into the model or cache the result.
Array de-dupe one-liner: [...new Set(arr)] removes duplicates while preserving order.
Controlled vs uncontrolled inputs: a controlled input's value comes from state (value + onChange); an uncontrolled one reads from a ref on submit.
Truncate text with an ellipsis: white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; on a fixed-width element.
Dismiss the keyboard in SwiftUI with @FocusState and set the focused field to nil.
structuredClone(obj) deep-copies most objects natively -- no more JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)) round-trips.
useRef holds a mutable value that persists across renders WITHOUT causing a re-render when it changes — reach for it for timers, DOM nodes, or the previous value of something.
Derive, don't sync: if a value can be computed from props or state during render, compute it there instead of storing it in state and updating it from a useEffect.
State updates are asynchronous and batched — the variable won't change on the next line. Read the new value on the next render, or use the functional updater setX(prev => ...).
Fetching in useEffect? Guard the response race: set an ignore flag (or use AbortController) in the cleanup so a slow earlier request can't overwrite newer data.
Keep hooks unconditional: always call them at the top level, never inside if statements or loops, so their order stays stable across every render.
